key_big: Resting potential −70 mV; Na⁺ in during an impulse.

body_html:
How to think about it

A neuron has dendrites, a cell body and an axon. At rest the inside is about −70 mV, kept by the Na⁺/K⁺ pump. A stimulus opens Na⁺ channels (depolarisation), then K⁺ leaves (repolarisation); in myelinated fibres the impulse jumps between nodes of Ranvier. At a synapse a neurotransmitter such as acetylcholine crosses the cleft.

The brain has the forebrain (cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus), midbrain and hindbrain (pons, cerebellum, medulla). Reflexes are fast automatic responses through the spinal cord. The eye has rods and cones in the retina; the ear's cochlea is for hearing and the semicircular canals for balance.

Example

Part of brain for balance?

hindbrain

Answer: cerebellum

Example

Ion entering during an impulse?

depolarisation

Answer: Na⁺

Common mistakes

  • Saying K⁺ enters during depolarisation.
  • Calling the medulla the seat of thinking.
  • Saying cones work best in dim light.
